news.title: Uefa threatens Fifa with legal action over World Cup plan, Infantino sought Trump’s backing
news.lede: Fifa president Gianni Infantino sought support ⁠from the Trump ⁠administration amid mounting criticism ⁠after his abandoned plan to sell a stake in World Cup commercial rights, the New York Post said on Monday, citing sources familiar with the matter. European football body Uefa, meanwhile, has threatened football’s governing body with legal action over Infantino’s failed plan, and said any potential evidence should not be destroyed. And in more bad news for the Fifa chief, the English Football Association is set to write to Infantino withdrawing its support amid the fallout, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) has already withdrawn its support and German Football Federation (DFB) managing director Andreas Rettig said the relationship between the association and football’s governing body was beyond repair.

news.title: Fifa president: Who might replace Gianni Infantino in world football's top job?
news.lede: Victor Montagliani, Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa and Mattias Grafstrom are among those who could succeed Gianni Infantino as Fifa president. It feels as though the walls are closing in on Fifa president Gianni Infantino. The Swiss is in a lonely place after scrapping controversial plans to sell off stakes in Fifa competitions to private investment. As it stands, Infantino will stand for re-election in March as he targets a fourth and final term as president.

news.title: Watch & learn: 300 Chennai government school kids revisit 2026 FIFA World Cup
news.lede: CHENNAI: Around 300 children from 10 different government schools saw footage which had defining moments of the FIFA World Cup at the Tagore Film Centre here on Monday.The screening of the World Cup in US, Canada and Mexico, was done as part of grassroot football program Chennai Kaalpandhu League (CKL) and data engineering firm LatentView Analytics’s joint initiative to encourage children to learn what goes behind an elite footballer’s mind. Through a curated screening of memorable passages of play from the tournament, the students relived the spectacular goals of Kylian Mbappé, the magic of Lionel Messi and the artistry of Lamine Yamal on the big screen. Additionally, coaches from two-time ISL winners Chennaiyin FC showed what it takes to compete at the highest level. .
